text:
tara: hi all, tara here onboarding into runtime team. trying to build from source and hitting a linker error that references cublas. who should I bug for a quick sanity check?

emily: welcome! paste the error and OS/toolkit versions.

tara: error below:
```
ERROR: /home/tara/runtime/BUILD:101:1: Linking of rule '//runtime:serve' failed (Exit 1): gcc failed: error executing command ...
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcublas
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
INFO: Build completed, 1 target failed.
```
I installed CUDA 12.1 in /usr/local/cuda-12.1 via the package repo, `nvcc --version` shows release 12.1, nvidia-smi shows Driver Version: 525.60.13.

rick: `cannot find -lcublas` usually means the linker can't find libcublas.so in lib search paths. Check `ls /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcublas*` and `ldconfig -p | grep cublas`. Also confirm CUDA_HOME and LD_LIBRARY_PATH point to /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64.

tara: `ls` shows libcublas.so.12 and libcublas.so.12.0.0 present. `ldconfig -p | grep cublas` returns nothing. I didn't run ldconfig after installing.

pete: try `sudo ldconfig` then `ldconfig -p | grep cublas`. If bazel still can't link, add `-L/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64` to linkopts in your `.bazelrc` or set `BAZEL_LINKOPTS`. Also check if a conda env is messing with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` — conda can unset/override.

tara: ran `sudo ldconfig` and now `ldconfig -p | grep cublas` shows libcublas.so.12 -> /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcublas.so.12. Re-running bazel build still failing but now a different error:
```
/usr/bin/ld: /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcublas.so.12: undefined symbol: __cudaPopCallConfiguration
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

emily: that undefined symbol often means libcuda/libcudart versions are mismatched between userland and kernel module or you have multiple CUDA installs. Run `ldd /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcublas.so.12 | grep cuda` and `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` and `nvidia-smi`.

tara: `ldd` shows libcudart.so.12 -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so.12 (from 525). `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` -> libcuda.so.1 -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (525). nvidia-smi ok.

rick: hmm ok driver and toolkit seem aligned. Another common culprit: stale copies on PATH or LD_LIBRARY_PATH (eg from older /opt/cuda). `readlink -f $(which nvcc)` and `echo $LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Also check for symbolic link collisions: sometimes distro packages put wrappers in /usr/lib that are incompatible.

tara: `which nvcc` -> /usr/local/cuda-12.1/bin/nvcc. LD_LIBRARY_PATH empty. No other cuda dirs found in `ls /opt`.

pete: one more thing: are you building with `-fPIC` for any hand-compiled libs? The symbol `__cudaPopCallConfiguration` is part of device runtime; if something linked against a different cuda runtime ABI (eg compiled with CUDA toolkit 11.x headers) you can see this. Try `nm -D /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcublas.so.12 | grep cudaPopCall` to confirm symbol presence. If it's missing, your libcublas may be corrupted; consider reinstalling the CUDA toolkit or using the dev container image (gcr.io/redwood-runtime/dev:cuda-12.1-2025-02).

tara: `nm -D` shows the symbol present. I spun up the dev container and the build works there. So seems host environment odd. I'll try reinstalling CUDA toolkit from the runfile and re-run `sudo ldconfig`, plus bazel clean.

devx-bot: DevX tip: For runtime builds, we recommend using the verified dev container image to avoid host driver/toolkit mismatch. If you must use host, follow the "Runtime host GPU setup" doc and run `sudo ldconfig` after installs, `bazel clean --expunge` after env changes, and file an infra ticket if kernel module/driver mismatch persists. If blocked >2h, page #oncall-runtime.

tara: switching to runfile reinstall now; will update thread. thanks everyone for the pointers. :raised_hands:
